object_types.name: Patient
object_types.definition: A person who books appointments at the clinic

source_references.excerpt: Patients book appointments. Every appointment is booked by exactly one patient, and a patient can have many appointments... Patients have a patient ID -- it's on their card.

object_types.name: PatientId
object_types.definition: The unique identifier for a patient, recorded on their card

source_references.excerpt: Patients have a patient ID -- it's on their card.

object_types.name: Doctor
object_types.definition: A medical professional who sees patients in appointments

source_references.excerpt: Each appointment is with exactly one doctor. Doctors see many patients across their appointments... Doctors have a license number.

object_types.name: LicenseNumber
object_types.definition: The unique medical license number that identifies a doctor

source_references.excerpt: Doctors have a license number.

object_types.name: Appointment
object_types.definition: A scheduled meeting between a patient and a doctor at the clinic

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment is booked by exactly one patient... Appointments get an appointment number when they're created.

object_types.name: AppointmentNumber
object_types.definition: The unique identifier assigned to an appointment when it is created

source_references.excerpt: Appointments get an appointment number when they're created.

object_types.name: ExamRoom
object_types.definition: A room at the clinic used for patient examinations

source_references.excerpt: Exam rooms have a room number.

object_types.name: RoomNumber
object_types.definition: The unique identifier for an exam room

source_references.excerpt: Exam rooms have a room number.

object_types.name: Specialty
object_types.definition: A medical specialty such as cardiology or general practice

source_references.excerpt: Every doctor has exactly one specialty, like cardiology or general practice.

object_types.name: AppointmentDate
object_types.definition: The calendar date on which an appointment is scheduled

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment is on a date and at a time slot -- we book in fixed slots like 09:00 or 09:30.

object_types.name: TimeSlot
object_types.definition: A fixed time slot for appointments, such as 09:00 or 09:30

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment is on a date and at a time slot -- we book in fixed slots like 09:00 or 09:30.

object_types.name: AppointmentStatus
object_types.definition: The current status of an appointment

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment also has a status. The status is one of: scheduled, checked-in, completed, or cancelled. Never. An appointment always has exactly one status from that list.

ambiguities.description: Exam room usage is unspecified. The transcript introduces ExamRoom as an entity type with a room number identifier, but does not describe any relationship between appointments and exam rooms. Are appointments assigned to specific exam rooms? Is this an optional assignment, or is every appointment in a specific room? This needs clarification to determine if a fact type 'Appointment is in ExamRoom' should be added.

source_references.excerpt: Exam rooms have a room number.

ambiguities.description: Visit reason cardinality on value constraint. The transcript states 'An appointment can have a visit reason' (line 27), indicating visit reason is optional. However, it does not specify whether a given visit reason text can be reused across multiple appointments (many-to-many) or if each visit reason instance is unique to an appointment. Is 'VisitReason' meant to be an enumerated list of standard reasons, or free-form text provided by the patient? This affects whether VisitReason should have a value constraint with predefined choices.

source_references.excerpt: An appointment can have a visit reason the patient gives when booking

ambiguities.description: Follow-up note reusability. Similar to visit reason, the transcript does not clarify whether a follow-up note can be attached to multiple appointments. The phrase 'the doctor can attach a follow-up note' (line 27) followed by 'At most one follow-up note per appointment' (line 27) implies one note per appointment, but does not clarify if multiple appointments can share the same note text or if each is independent.

source_references.excerpt: after the visit the doctor can attach a follow-up note. At most one follow-up note per appointment.

ambiguities.description: Appointment date-time uniqueness. The transcript specifies that appointments have both a date and a time slot, but does not state whether the combination of date and time slot is unique per doctor, per exam room, or globally across all appointments. Can two doctors each have an appointment at 09:00 on the same day? Can the same doctor have appointments in the same time slot on different dates? These constraints need clarification.

source_references.excerpt: Every appointment is on a date and at a time slot -- we book in fixed slots like 09:00 or 09:30.
